findings.lawNote: Law 1 overrides Law 2. The implementation is faithful; the STORY'S OWN INTENT is what enables the loss, so this is filed against the story, not against the executor.
findings.specText: story-003 Technical Details line 65-68: "`if (mintedForStable + amount < minPhUSDOut) revert InsufficientPhUSDOut(minPhUSDOut, mintedForStable + amount);` ... So `mintedForStable + amount` is the total phUSD delivered to `recipient` - the identical value already emitted as the event's final field at line 263". story-003 Technical Details line 45-52 (the DELETE instruction): "Lines to DELETE (`src/Antimatter.sol:232-235`): `uint256 expectedForStable = minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount); if (expectedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();`". story-003 Concerns line 140: "**`minPhUSDOut == 0` is permitted**: it waives the caller's own protection rather than exposing the protocol". story-003 Implementation Notes line 86: "A caller passing `minPhUSDOut == 0` at a zero rate would receive only the antimatter half."
findings.actualBehavior: Implemented exactly as written. At src/Antimatter.sol:259-260 the floor is compared against `totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable`, and `amount` phUSD is minted for the antimatter half unconditionally at :263. `mintedForStable` is a uint256, so `totalPhUSD >= amount` always holds and the predicate `totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut` is UNSATISFIABLE for every `minPhUSDOut` in [0, amount] - not merely for zero. The protection a caller actually buys is `minPhUSDOut - amount`, which is <= 0 across that whole range. Meanwhile `mintedForStable == amount * R / 1e18` exactly (decimals cancel), so at R == 0 the caller's stablecoin half is pulled (:246), approved and consumed by `minter.mint` (:251) and deposited one-way into the yield strategy, and the caller receives only the 1x antimatter half - with no revert and no on-chain trace that a floor was ever stated (`Annihilated` at :266 logs `totalPhUSD` but not `minPhUSDOut`).
findings.deviation: Not a deviation - a defect in the intended design. Three of the story's stated decisions are challenged: (1) The story instructs deletion of `if (expectedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();` as part of removing 'quote duplication'. It is not duplication: that guard was the ONLY protocol-side liveness check that the stablecoin half fetched anything at all, and it is orthogonal to the exactness check the story set out to remove. The story deletes it in the same breath as the quote lookup without ever justifying that leg separately. (2) The story chooses the COMBINED total as the floor's unit and justifies that choice by symmetry with the event field (line 68) - a presentation convenience - even though the only leg that can move is the stable half. That choice is what creates the inert band: a caller expressing the floor in the natural unit ('my stable half must fetch at least X') lands inside [0, amount] and silently buys nothing. Correct usage requires `minPhUSDOut = amount + expectedStableHalf`, which the NatSpec at :222-225 states but which inverts the intuitive unit. (3) The story's Concerns confine the waiver to `minPhUSDOut == 0` (lines 86, 140) and reason that a waiver 'is the caller's own protection'. That reasoning does not survive the arithmetic: the waiver is not opt-in at a single sentinel value, it is the default across a contiguous range of apparently-meaningful values, and the contract neither rejects nor records an inert floor (no `require(minPhUSDOut > amount)`, `minPhUSDOut` absent from the event).
findings.footgunAnalysis: Law 3 test - would a competent, NON-MALICIOUS operator or an honest caller be surprised? Yes, on both sides. No attacker is required; no malicious owner is posited. R == 0 is reachable through ordinary non-malicious operation (a stablecoin registered before its exchange rate is set, or a rate mid-update), and the continuous partial shortfall `amount * (1e18 - R) / 1e18` is reachable for every R in (0, 1e18). Before this delta both cases were caught protocol-side; now neither is. NON-OBVIOUS footgun => in scope.
findings.impact: Loss of the caller's entire stablecoin half (irreversibly deposited into the yield strategy; PhusdStableMinter exposes no redeem/burn/withdraw path) against delivery of only the 1x antimatter half, on a call that succeeded while the caller believed a floor was enforced. Assets are user funds; the loss requires the external condition of an adverse/zero rate, which places it at C4 Medium (value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements) rather than High.
findings.ledgerCorrespondence: NEW as a story-level finding, but it is the Law-1 view of the SAME root cause as tier-2 CODE-001 (proposed rootCauseClass CombinedTotalFloorInertBelowAmount) and ECON-001. It must NOT mint a competing third fingerprint: downstream dedup should collapse these three into ONE entry, retaining CODE-001's proposed fingerprint basis `src/Antimatter.sol:annihilate:CombinedTotalFloorInertBelowAmount` and attaching this story text as evidence for the story-unsafe framing and for the severity argument. It is NOT a re-file of F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060) - see the F-01 reconciliation below.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Either (a) measure the floor against the stable leg alone (`if (mintedForStable < minPhUSDOut)`), which restores a monotone, intuitively-unitised guarantee; or (b) keep the combined total and add `if (minPhUSDOut <= amount) revert InertFloor(minPhUSDOut, amount);` so an inert floor fails loudly; and in either case restore a protocol-side `mintedForStable == 0` revert, which is not caller-waivable and costs nothing when the rate is healthy. Add `minPhUSDOut` to the `Annihilated` event so an honoured floor is distinguishable from an inert one after the fact.

findings.specText: story-003 Test Impact line 98: "For tests not about slippage, pass `0` (or the exact expected total) - be consistent and say which in the code." Checklist lines 128-129: "Add a test that a floor met exactly (`total == minPhUSDOut`) succeeds - boundary of `<`" and "Add a test that `minPhUSDOut == 0` disables the floor and the call succeeds". Autonomous Decision 4 line 232: "A zero floor is inert, so each of those tests still observes only the behaviour it is actually about."
findings.actualBehavior: The six floor tests sample minPhUSDOut only at 0 (test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor) and at values strictly above `amount` (the below-floor revert, the clearing-floor success, and the `total == minPhUSDOut` boundary). The other 24 call sites all pass 0 per Decision 4. No test in the suite passes a floor in the open band (0, amount] - and every assertion of test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor would hold unchanged for any value in that band.
findings.deviation: The story's boundary coverage is written against the `<` operator rather than against the semantic boundary that matters, which is `minPhUSDOut == amount` - the point where the floor stops being inert. Decision 4's rationale ('a zero floor is inert') is true but incomplete for the same arithmetic reason as F-05, and the executor's uniform-0 convention means the suite cannot distinguish 'the floor was honoured' from 'the floor could not fire'. The story's own PASSED review cited these tests as proof the floor works.
findings.impact: Test-coverage gap only - no direct loss. It is filed because it is the mechanism by which F-05 passed a green 69/0 suite and a PASSED review. A regression test at `minPhUSDOut == amount` would have failed to revert and exposed F-05 immediately.
findings.ledgerCorrespondence: GENUINELY NEW. Proposed fingerprint basis `test/Annihilation.t.sol:floorSuite:InertBandUnsampled`. Do not collapse into F-05 - one is the defect, the other is why the suite did not catch it - but if the dedup tier prefers a single entry, F-05 is the survivor and this becomes a sub-note of it, never the reverse.

ledgerReconciliations.label: F-01
ledgerReconciliations.reasoning: story-003 IS the fix for F-01 ('no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn'). A minimum-output parameter now exists, so F-01's literal wording is satisfied and a diff-driven or grep-driven pass would read the fix as landed. It is not: the guard the fix installs is provably unable to fire for any `minPhUSDOut` in [0, amount], it is opt-out by default, no code path requires it to be set to a meaningful value, and nothing protocol-side replaced the two checks (`expectedForStable == 0` and the exactness comparison) that were deleted to make room for it. Per the repository's own rule, a fix that reads as done while the underlying exposure survives ranks second only to a regression. Annotate the entry `incompleteFixOf` and point it at F-05. Human applies any status change; this run only proposes.

ledgerReconciliations.label: F-02
ledgerReconciliations.verdict: WORSENED by this delta - stays open, re-weigh candidate at the top of Low
ledgerReconciliations.reasoning: F-02 says the CLAUDE.md-nominated trip-wire for 'Antimatter must never expose a burn' is a four-name denylist rather than an invariant check. This delta demonstrates the brittleness concretely and makes it worse. test/Annihilation.t.sol:457-458 still reads `["burn(uint256)", "burn(address,uint256)", "burnFrom(address,uint256)", "annihilate(address,uint256)"]`. Story-003 changed the real entry point's selector for the SECOND time in three stories, and per its own instruction (line 90: 'update the comment text only, never the assertions') only the comment at :454-456 was touched. The consequence: the list still names `annihilate(address,uint256)`, a form that has never existed in this contract, while `annihilate(address,address,uint256)` - story-001's own signature, which DID exist at c91bc1a and is now absent - is not named, and no assertion in the suite tracks the entry point's identity at all. The denylist is now demonstrably decoupled from the invariant it is nominated to enforce: it would keep passing across any future signature change, including one that added a burn-reaching path. Reconcile to the existing fingerprint; the story's compliance with line 90 was correct and is not itself a finding.

ledgerReconciliations.label: F-03
ledgerReconciliations.verdict: UNCHANGED LINES, MATERIALLY MORE WRONG CLAIM - explicit re-weigh, stays open
ledgerReconciliations.proposedStatus: open, re-weigh to the top of Low with a rewritten description; escalate only if the classifier collapses it into F-05
ledgerReconciliations.reasoning: This is the finding a diff-driven pass would miss, so it is stated explicitly. F-03's cited lines - the contract-header NatSpec, and the repo spec at lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md:99 ('antimatter's entire value to a holder is that it annihilates into phUSD worth twice its quantity') - are byte-for-byte unchanged by this delta. Its CLAIM is not. At c91bc1a a settled annihilation was anchored on both sides: `expectedForStable == 0` reverted the exact-zero-rate case pre-burn, and the exactness comparison forced the stable leg to equal the minter's own quote, so the documented 2x, while never guaranteed at par, could not degrade all the way to 1x without reverting. After 3a96fb7 both anchors are gone: `mintedForStable == amount * R / 1e18` is accepted at whatever R the minter holds, and at R == 0 the 1x endpoint SETTLES where it previously reverted. The gap between CLAUDE.md:99 and the code is therefore no longer a matter of rounding and par - the documented value proposition's floor case is now a reachable, silent, non-reverting outcome. story-003's checklist item at line 131 asserts 'no change needed' for CLAUDE.md lines 93/95/99/110 on the ground that the never-expose-a-burn and settles-whole-or-not-at-all invariants still hold. That is correct for lines 93/95/110 and for both invariants, but it does not answer for line 99, which states a value property rather than an invariant and which the grep the story performed ('no mention of calculateMintAmount, of a quote, or of the annihilate signature') could not have surfaced. RECONCILE TO 9d06644ddad24e5a - do not mint a new fingerprint for the 2x claim.

ledgerReconciliations.verdict: MOOT BY DELETION - propose fixed (human applies)
ledgerReconciliations.reasoning: F-04 objects to the untagged commit c91bc1a ('more precise mint requirement') rewriting the annihilation settlement post-condition on top of a two-story stack. Story-003 has deleted exactly the code that commit introduced: `expectedForStable`/`PhUSDNotReceived` and the `mintedForStable != expectedForStable` exactness check no longer exist at 3a96fb7 (grep over src/ finds no residual reference to `calculateMintAmount`, `PhUSDNotReceived` or `PhUSDAmountMismatch`). The code the finding is about is gone, deliberately and under a story that names it, so the finding has no live substance. Note this is a moot-by-deletion closure, NOT a verified fix of a defect - the disposition should say so on the entry. Two residues survive the closure and are recorded here rather than dropped: (a) story-001's acceptance checklist still self-certifies that the settlement logic it forbade touching was preserved, which remains untrue of the historical record; (b) the process gap F-04 names has recurred in a new form in this very delta - see F-07 - so closing F-04 should not be read as the process concern being retired.
